lectures.title: Displaying a Location Preview Map Snapshot via Google

cues.en: Now, to show a preview,
we'll use the Google Maps Static API,
which is simply another API offered by Google
under that Google Maps umbrella, so to say.
And that's a very simple API,
which we can use to create snapshots of locations on a map,
so images of a certain place on a map, you could say.
Now, on this page here,
you'll find an example for the kind of URL
you must construct to generate such a snapshot
because it's basically an image
that is created on the fly
based on the configuration you set up in this URL here.
And I'll copy this URL therefore,
and I'll use that for generating such a preview.
And we don't need to generate the preview here
where we get the location.
Instead, as I just said, it's basically a URL
that directly leads to an image
that will be created on the fly.
Therefore, we can directly output that image with a widget.
And I'll simply add a getter
which will contain this URL here,
so that we don't need
to put this long URL into our widget tree.
Instead, here in the _LocationInputState class,
I'll add a new getter that will return a string
because in the end it simply will return this URL
with all the necessary data plucked into it.
And I'll name my getter LocationImage
because in the end, again, it will provide a URL,
a link to an image.
And I'll simply return that string here
as a string, of course,
but now we have to plug in all the necessary data.
And of course that's a very long string
and you should make sure that it's all in one line,
but we will also shorten it here, no worries.
Because for example here,
this center part,
which here for me by default is sent
to Brooklyn+Bridge,New+York,NY,
should be replaced
with the latitude and longitude coordinates.
So for that here in the getter,
we can get the latitude
by reaching out to the picked location
and accessing the latitude there.
And the same, of course, for the longitude,
which we also get from the picked location
and then longitude.
Now, here, I actually can be certain
that this will not be null
because I'll only use this URL if we are showing a preview,
which we will only do down there,
at least soon, if we have a picked place.
But we could also add an extra check here
where we check if (_pickedLocation == null),
in which case we could return an empty string here
if we wanted to,
then we can be super certain
that this will not be null.
So with that, we got latitude and longitude,
and this should now be injected into this string
after center here,
so that we have lat, comma, and then longitude.
Now, the zoom level, I'll set this to 16.
And for the size here, I'll keep 600x300.
This simply defines the size of the image
that will be generated,
and it's width times height.
Now, for the map type,
we wanna keep a roadmap,
but now for the markers,
we can delete a lot of stuff here.
With that marker's configuration here,
you simply configure which markers
will be part of that image,
so you control which pins will be on the map.
And here, I want to have a marker,
but only one.
Therefore, you can delete all other &markers parts
with all their configuration except for the first one,
and that will make that URL way shorter.
So everything up to &key is deleted here
because we will still need to add our API key here later.
And then here, for that one marker that we kept,
you can choose the color
and you can choose from those base colors
like red, blue, and so on.
So here, I'll pick red.
Now, the label here simply defines which character
is shown in the marker,
and I'll simply pick A.
And then thereafter you have this %7C separator,
which you should keep.
But then you again have the latitude
where the marker should be placed,
and that, of course, should be the same latitude
as is the center of this place,
and the longitude.
And here I just saw that after center,
we should have an equal sign.
But with that back on the marker,
that should be the marker configuration.
And now we just also need to add the API key,
which we also are using down here,
so it's the same API key.
Copy that and inject that here.
And then we can delete this signature part here,
it's not required.
And with that, we have a getter
that generates such a snapshot URL
that should be usable as an image.
And therefore as a next step,
we can go down to the widget.
And there I now wanna check
if we have a _pickedLocation,
so if this is not null,
and in that case, previewContent
should be set equal to an Image widget
using the network constructor
because we're now fetching an image over the network
via that URL that is returned by our getter.
So here I'll refer to my locationImage getter
that we just added,
and I'll add fit : BoxFit.cover,
and make sure that we use the full width
with double infinity
and height with double infinity
inside of that container that we're using.
And the container we're using
is, of course, that container
that has previewContent as a child.
And with that, we should be showing a preview of our place
after it was picked.
Now, at the moment, we won't really be able to test this
because we have a couple of errors in our code

And to be able to test this,

So back here in the app,

Let's see if it eventually finishes.
Looking good,
it shows a location.
